text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any redness, warmth, or significant pain in the knee, and does he have a history of excessive bleeding from minor cuts or after vaccinations? I would also like to check his current coagulation profile. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Profile

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No overlying skin redness noted; swelling is warm to touch. Coagulation profile results: ACT 52.0 s (prolonged), PT 14.0 s, Thrombin time < 2 seconds deviation from control.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged activated clotting time with a normal prothrombin time suggests a defect in the intrinsic pathway, such as Hemophilia A or B. To distinguish between these possibilities, I need to check the specific factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal Factor VIII level and the intrinsic pathway defect, I suspect Hemophilia B. REQUEST TEST: Factor_IX_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor IX level: 5% (Low; normal range 50-150%)

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Factor IX level confirms a diagnosis of Hemophilia B. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia B
